promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

A pure metal
An alloy of copper and zinc
A ferrous metal that rusts easily
questions.explain: Brass is an alloy made by combining copper and zinc, giving it good corrosion resistance and machinability.

questions.q: Corrugated cardboard is widely used for packaging mainly because it is:
options: Waterproof and conducts heat well
Extremely heavy and rigid like steel
A natural timber
Lightweight, low-cost and provides good impact protection
questions.explain: The fluted middle layer of corrugated card gives strength and cushioning while keeping the board light and cheap, ideal for protective packaging.

questions.q: 'Reduce' in the 6 Rs encourages designers and users to:
options: Use more material to be safe
Send waste to landfill faster
Buy more products overall
Use less material and energy to make and run a product
questions.explain: Reduce focuses on minimising the amount of material and energy used in making and using a product.

questions.q: Malleability is the property that allows a material to be:
options: Hammered or rolled into thin sheets without cracking
Returned to its original shape after a force is removed
Scratched easily
Stretched into a long wire
questions.explain: Malleability is the ability of a material to be deformed by compression, such as hammering or rolling into sheets, without breaking.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between thermoforming and thermosetting polymers?
options: Thermosetting polymers can be reheated and reshaped; thermoforming polymers cannot
Neither type can be shaped by heat
Thermoforming polymers can be reheated and reshaped; thermosetting polymers cannot
Both can be reheated and reshaped equally
questions.explain: Thermoforming (thermoplastic) polymers soften when heated and can be reshaped repeatedly, while thermosetting polymers set permanently and cannot be remelted.

questions.q: Recycling differs from reusing because recycling:
options: Refuses to use the material at all
Means throwing the item away
Uses a product again in its current form
Processes a material to make a new product
questions.explain: Recycling reprocesses a material into raw form to make a new product, whereas reusing keeps the original item in use as it is.

questions.q: In the 6 Rs of sustainability, 'Refuse' means to:
options: Throw a product into landfill
Recycle the material into something new
Decline to buy or use something you do not really need
Repair a broken product
questions.explain: Refuse means choosing not to buy or use products or materials that are unnecessary or wasteful in the first place.

questions.q: An ethical concern when sourcing materials globally is:
options: Adding more electronic components
Making the product as colourful as possible
Choosing the heaviest packaging
Ensuring workers are paid fairly and not exploited
questions.explain: Ethical sourcing considers whether the people who extract or make materials are treated and paid fairly.

questions.q: Carbon-fibre reinforced polymer is an example of a composite because it:
options: Can be melted and remoulded endlessly
Is a single pure element
Combines two or more materials to gain improved properties
Is a naturally occurring timber
questions.explain: A composite combines two or more different materials, such as carbon fibres in a resin matrix, to achieve a high strength-to-weight ratio.

questions.q: Which is a natural fibre rather than a synthetic one?
options: Cotton
Nylon
Polyester
Acrylic
questions.explain: Cotton is a natural fibre grown from the cotton plant, whereas polyester, nylon and acrylic are synthetic fibres made from polymers.

questions.q: Choosing a material that can be recycled at the end of a product's life supports sustainability by:
options: Keeping materials in use and reducing demand for new raw resources
Increasing the amount of waste sent to landfill
Making the product impossible to dispose of
Guaranteeing the product never wears out
questions.explain: Recyclable materials can be recovered and reprocessed, reducing landfill and the need to extract new raw materials.

questions.q: Plywood is made stronger and more stable than solid timber by:
options: Adding only metal to the surface
Soaking the wood in water
Removing all the natural fibres
Gluing thin veneers with the grain of each layer at right angles to the next
questions.explain: Plywood is built from layers of veneer bonded with the grain of each layer running at right angles, which resists warping and adds strength in both directions.
